identity.title: Quercetin suppresses radial glial stem-like cell functions through an HSPB1-associated mechanism in glioma.

content.abstract: Glioma is a highly malignant tumor characterized by pronounced intratumoral heterogeneity. By integrating multi-omics analyses, we identified radial glial stem-like (RG-like) cells as a putative upstream developmental-like state in inferred glioma differentiation trajectories. Integrated spatial transcriptomic and histopathological analyses further linked the molecular features of RG-like cells to their spatial distribution and associated tissue morphology. A CRISPR-based knockout screen highlighted heat shock protein beta-1 (HSPB1) as a potential molecular target associated with RG-like cell functions. We subsequently investigated quercetin (QUE) and found that it inhibited glioma cell growth and suppressed mitotic somal translocation (MST), a characteristic RG-like cellular behavior. Mechanistic analyses showed that QUE reduced HSPB1 protein expression and was associated with a reduced detectable interaction between HSPB1 and vimentin (VIM). Together, these findings characterize RG-like cells at the molecular and histopathological levels and suggest that QUE may represent a potential pharmacological approach for modulating their associated functions in glioma.
